name: ZenZap
summary: Secure work-chat for teams — organized channels, built-in tasks and workflows, AI agents and admin controls, as easy to use as texting.
best_for: small teams that run work over messy WhatsApp/personal chat today and want organized, professional chat with tasks — starting free
skip_if: your workflows depend on a deep integration ecosystem (Slack's moat), or you're already paid into Microsoft Teams via 365
honest_knock: The pricing genuinely undercuts Slack — the honest question is ecosystem: team chat lives or dies on integrations and habit, and ZenZap's app catalog is a fraction of Slack's, so teams glued to hundreds of integrations will feel the gap. For WhatsApp-refugee teams that mainly need organized channels, tasks and work/life separation, the free tier is a remarkably complete landing spot.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month in total for up to 20 users billed yearly ($63 monthly)
pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-10-07 on the vendor's own pricing page; unchanged on 2026-10-15) The per-seat prices are gone. On 1 September the page sold Pro at $3 a user a month billed yearly ($4 monthly) and Business+ at $8 ($10 monthly), with flat team bundles beside them; our 1 October capture and the page on 7 October sell flat monthly packages only, in two tabs. Under 'Just chat': Free at $0, 'forever free for your whole team', with group chats and DMs, built-in to-dos, scheduled messages, calendar integration, WhatsApp chat migration, team access and permissions, malware scanning of files, 1 GB of storage, AI voice-note transcription and in-chat search; and Lite at $51 a month in total for up to 20 users on annual billing ($63 month to month), adding voice and video calls, task templates and sub-tasks, team privacy and download controls, group-creation permissions, 100 GB of storage, AI workspace search and turning messages into tasks. Under 'AI agents in chat': Free at $0 with 'every feature, every integration', unlimited users and 100 AI credits a month; and Business+ at $50 a month in total for up to 5 users on annual billing ($62 month to month) with 400 AI credits a month, AI work agents for every user, automated workflows, third-party agents, API access, call recording with transcription and 10 TB of storage. Enterprise is custom in both tabs and carries SAML, SCIM and SSO, encryption key management and audit logs. Add-ons are listed without prices: extra AI credits, extra storage, an HR-system integration and HIPAA compliance with a signed BAA. External guests such as clients and contractors do not count toward a plan's user limit. The page says annual billing saves up to 33%; the two cards we read save about 19%. The cards print no price for more users than the package covers, so ask before you plan a bigger rollout.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 on a new workspace with data in Europe, without a card, without connecting a calendar or other tools and without inviting team members: Daan signed up with a phone number and SMS code, and our AI assistant set up the workspace in Daan's browser through the web app. We made a group, posted a message with a test code, turned it into a to-do with a due date, searched for the code and completed the to-do. Plan name: not recorded.
findings: Sign-up works only with a mobile number and a six-digit SMS code ('Sign in with email' is for existing users). Onboarding now presents Zenzap as an agent platform: after the workspace it asks who you are building agents for, your company size, role, industry and tools, and you must create your first agent (a name and an avatar) before you reach the chat. Skipping team invites asks for confirmation ('Start without your team?'). No card or sales call.

A message becomes a to-do through the message menu (⋮ > Add to-do): it appears in the To-do panel next to the chat and as a card in the chat. A due date is set with a calendar (time optional, with 'Show in my calendar'), and the chat logs each change. The checkbox next to a message only selects it for forwarding or replying; it does not create a to-do.

Searching the test code found 3 hits, all under 'Messages': the message itself, the 'added to-do' event and the 'Set due date' event. There was no separate group for to-dos in the results, and an 'AI' button sits next to search.
Ticking off the to-do moved it to 'Completed to-do's' with strikethrough, the chat logged 'marked as Done', and Library > To-do's then showed 0 open.
The new workspace already held 'My Personal Space', a general channel, a welcome message from a Zenzap staff member and a message from our own agent.
